Figure 1:Overview ofParetoRSI-Gym.
Starting from a fixed initial model, an agent curates post-training data for five domains over repeated rounds.
In each round the current principles direct which datasets the agent searches for and pulls from HuggingFace, and which entries it keeps; the resulting entries are committed to a persistent pool, which is submitted for fine-tuning and tested on the per-domain benchmarks; the scores are then used to update the principles for the next round.
Success requires the capability vector to expand on every domain at once rather than on a single target.

Table 3:Main results ofParetoRSI-Gymon the generalization benchmarks.Each cell is the score followed by its change in points from theM0M_{0}row of its block, the model before any curation.Proxy Bestis the round whose average proxy score is the highest, andDomain Besttakes each domain from its own best round, so it is not a deployable checkpoint.
Proprietary systems are run with three seeds(Rank et al., 2026)and we report the mean.

Figure 3:What the agents train on.(a) Jaccard overlap of the datasets used by each pair of runs; blocks group runs by agent.
(b) Share of each round’s training pool going to each domain, averaged over runs.
(c) Datasets entering the training pool for the first time in each round, averaged over runs.
